title: A power series ring over a characteristic-zero field or a Cohen ring is formally smooth for its maximal-ideal-adic topology
statement: Let $n\ge0$. (1) Let $K$ be a field of characteristic $0$, $C=K[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$ the formal power series ring [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series], regarded as a $\mathbf Q$-algebra through $\mathbf Q\subseteq K\subseteq C$, and $\mathfrak m_C=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)\subseteq C$. Then $C$ is formally smooth over $\mathbf Q$ for the $\mathfrak m_C$-adic topology [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic]. (2) Let $p$ be a prime, $\Lambda$ a Cohen ring with residue characteristic $p$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring], $C=\Lambda[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$ and $\mathfrak m_C=(p,x_1,\ldots,x_n)\subseteq C$. Then $C$ is formally smooth over $\mathbf Z$ for the $\mathfrak m_C$-adic topology.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NL (lemma-power-series-ring-over-Cohen-fs, line 9704), parts (1) and (3); part (2) (F_p -> L[[x]]) is not stated here. Its proof reduces by the universal property of power series rings to Q -> K formally smooth (Algebra, Proposition Tag 0322, proposition-characterize-separable-field-extensions) and Z -> Lambda formally smooth for the m_Lambda-adic topology (Algebra, Lemma Tag 0329, lemma-cohen-ring-formally-smooth).

proof.text: *The test datum.* In both parts write $\Lambda_0$ for the coefficient ring ($\Lambda_0=K$ in (1), $\Lambda_0=\Lambda$ in (2)), $R$ for the base ($R=\mathbf Q$ in (1), $R=\mathbf Z$ in (2)) and $C=\Lambda_0[[x_1,\ldots,x_n]]$ [def-weil-pbc-multivariate-power-series]. By [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic] we must show: given a commutative ring $D$ with a ring map $R\to D$, an ideal $J\subseteq D$ with $J^2=0$, the quotient map $q:D\to D/J$ [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient], and a homomorphism of $R$-algebras $g:C\to D/J$ with $g(\mathfrak m_C^k)=0$ for some $k\ge1$, there is a homomorphism of $R$-algebras $f:C\to D$ with $q\circ f=g$. Fix such data. Since $q$ is surjective choose $d_i\in D$ with $q(d_i)=g(x_i)$, $i=1,\ldots,n$. As $x_i\in\mathfrak m_C$, $q(d_i^k)=g(x_i^k)=0$, so $d_i^k\in J$ and $d_i^{2k}\in J^2=0$. In (2) moreover $p\in\mathfrak m_C$ gives $q(p^k\cdot1_D)=g(p^k)=0$, so $p^k\cdot1_D\in J$ and $p^{2k}\cdot1_D=0$; put $d_0=p\cdot1_D$ in (2) and $d_0=0$ in (1). Let $\mathfrak a=(d_0,d_1,\ldots,d_n)\subseteq D$ and $M=(n+1)(2k-1)+1$. Every product of $M$ of the generators $d_0,\ldots,d_n$ contains some $d_i$ at least $2k$ times (pigeonhole), hence is $0$; so $\mathfrak a^M=0$, and likewise $\bar{\mathfrak a}^M=q(\mathfrak a)^M=q(\mathfrak a^M)=0$ in $D/J$ for $\bar{\mathfrak a}=q(\mathfrak a)$. A ring $T$ with an ideal $\mathfrak b$, $\mathfrak b^M=0$, is $\mathfrak b$-adically complete [def-weil-pbc-adically-complete-ring]: for $m\ge M$ the quotient $T/\mathfrak b^m$ is $T$ and the transition maps $T/\mathfrak b^{m+1}\to T/\mathfrak b^m$ are the identity of $T$, so the canonical map $T\to\varprojlim_mT/\mathfrak b^m$ is injective ($\bigcap_m\mathfrak b^m=0$) and surjective (a compatible family is determined by its component $a\in T/\mathfrak b^M=T$, and is then the image of $a$). Hence $D$ is $\mathfrak a$-adically complete and $D/J$ is $\bar{\mathfrak a}$-adically complete, and $d_i\in\mathfrak a$, $g(x_i)=q(d_i)\in\bar{\mathfrak a}$.

proof.text: *Lifting on the coefficients, part (1).* $K$ is a field of characteristic $0$ containing $\mathbf Q$, and $D$ is a $\mathbf Q$-algebra through $R\to D$. The restriction $g|_K:K\to D/J$ is a homomorphism of $\mathbf Q$-algebras (as $g$ is one and $\mathbf Q\subseteq K\subseteq C$). By [lem-weil-pbc-char-zero-field-extension-formally-smooth] for the extension $K/\mathbf Q$ (formal smoothness of $\mathbf Q\to K$, Algebra Proposition 0322), applied to $D$, $J$, $q$ and $g|_K$, there is a homomorphism of $\mathbf Q$-algebras $h:K\to D$ with $q\circ h=g|_K$.

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NL (lemma-power-series-ring-over-Cohen-fs, line 9704), proof (line 9718): reduction (1) '$\mathbf Q\to K$ is formally smooth', by Algebra, Proposition Tag 0322 (proposition-characterize-separable-field-extensions, algebra.tex line 44475)

proof.text: *Lifting on the coefficients, part (2).* Put $N=2k$. By Step 1, $p^N\cdot1_D=0$, so $D$ is a ring with $p^ND=0$; and $g(p^N)=g(p^k)g(p^k)=0$ (as $p^k\in\mathfrak m_C^k$), so the ring homomorphism $g|_\Lambda:\Lambda\to D/J$ kills $p^N\Lambda$ and factors as $g|_\Lambda=\bar g\circ\pi$ with $\pi:\Lambda\to\Lambda/p^N\Lambda$ the quotient map and $\bar g:\Lambda/p^N\Lambda\to D/J$ a ring homomorphism. By [lem-weil-pbc-cohen-ring-mod-pn-formally-smooth] for $\Lambda$ (a Cohen ring with residue characteristic $p$ [def-weil-pbc-cohen-ring]) and $n=N$, applied to $D$, $J$, $q$ and $\bar g$, there is a ring homomorphism $\bar f:\Lambda/p^N\Lambda\to D$ with $q\circ\bar f=\bar g$. Then $h=\bar f\circ\pi:\Lambda\to D$ is a ring homomorphism with $q\circ h=g|_\Lambda$. (This is the formal smoothness of $\mathbf Z\to\Lambda$ for the $p\Lambda$-adic topology, used by the source, in the instance needed.)

source.place: More on Algebra, Lemma Tag 07NL (lemma-power-series-ring-over-Cohen-fs, line 9704), proof (line 9718): reduction (3) '$\mathbf Z\to\Lambda$ is formally smooth in the $\mathfrak m_\Lambda$-adic topology', by Algebra, Lemma Tag 0329 (lemma-cohen-ring-formally-smooth, algebra.tex line 44907) since some power of $p$ is zero in $A$

proof.text: *Extension to the power series ring.* In both parts we now have a ring homomorphism $h:\Lambda_0\to D$ with $q\circ h=g|_{\Lambda_0}$ (Steps 2, 3). Apply [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-universal-property-complete] to $\Lambda_0$, $T=D$ (which is $\mathfrak a$-adically complete by Step 1), $\alpha=h$ and $t_i=d_i\in\mathfrak a$: there is a ring homomorphism $f:C\to D$ with $f|_{\Lambda_0}=h$ and $f(x_i)=d_i$. Now $q\circ f$ and $g$ are two ring homomorphisms $C\to D/J$; they agree on $\Lambda_0$ ($q\circ f|_{\Lambda_0}=q\circ h=g|_{\Lambda_0}$) and send $x_i$ to the same element $q(d_i)=g(x_i)\in\bar{\mathfrak a}$. Apply the uniqueness clause of [lem-weil-pbc-power-series-universal-property-complete] to $\Lambda_0$, $T=D/J$ (which is $\bar{\mathfrak a}$-adically complete by Step 1), $\alpha=g|_{\Lambda_0}$ and $t_i=g(x_i)$: hence $q\circ f=g$. Finally $f$ is a homomorphism of $R$-algebras [def-weil-pbc-algebra-hom-quotient]: in (2), $R=\mathbf Z$ and every ring homomorphism is $\mathbf Z$-linear; in (1), $f\circ(\mathbf Q\to C)$ and the structure map $\mathbf Q\to D$ are ring homomorphisms $\mathbf Q\to D$, and there is only one (it is determined on $\mathbf Z$ and $1/m$ must go to the inverse of $m\cdot1_D$).

proof.text: *Conclusion.* For every test datum $(D,J,g,k)$ of [def-weil-pbc-formally-smooth-adic] for $R\to C$ and the ideal $\mathfrak m_C$, Steps 1–4 give a homomorphism of $R$-algebras $f:C\to D$ with $q\circ f=g$. Hence $C$ is formally smooth over $\mathbf Q$ for the $\mathfrak m_C$-adic topology in (1) ($\mathfrak m_C=(x_1,\ldots,x_n)$, $d_0=0$), and over $\mathbf Z$ for the $\mathfrak m_C$-adic topology in (2) ($\mathfrak m_C=(p,x_1,\ldots,x_n)$).
